newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt prices continue rise, call money easy.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices continue rise, call money easy.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities continued to rise in brisk trade on Wednesday while call money remained stuck in a narrow range, dealers said.
They said good liquidity with banks and expectations of falling interest rates fuelled trade and pushed prices up.
Prices of government securities have been on the rise for the last fortnight as market players took positions in anticipation of a drop in interest rates, dealers said.

The Reserve Bank of India releases its monetary and credit policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) on April 15 amid market expectations that it will announce steps leading to a fall in interest rates.

"It (the rise in prices) is quite baffling..I don't know how much longer this can go on," said a money market dealer at a state-run bank. "Prices are already very high. In the long bond, maturing 2006, the yield has dropped by 50 basis points in just one fortnight."
A downward correction in prices was likely soon, he said.
"The rate of increase in prices of short-term paper is already slowing down," he added.
Dealers said call money ended Wednesday at 0.05-0.25 percent after opening around 3.0 percent.

"There were a couple of stray deals at 2.5 percent but most of the opening deals were at 1.5," said a dealer. "Rates fell once the market became aware that Monday's repo auction security was a zero-coupon bond."
"The outflow towards zero-coupon bonds is less than for other securities," he said.
He said market players had expected call rates to be around 2.0 percent after Monday's repo auction at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) accepted bids for 46.3 billion rupees.
"But once the market realised the stock sold by the RBI was the zero-coupon bond, rates fell sharply," the dealer said.
